comparator.academicYear: Current UvA published bachelor curriculum, checked 2026-09-27
comparator.sourceNotes: The official curriculum totals 60+60+60=180 EC. The ACVA A–D skills line is published without separate EC and is integrated into the credited curriculum. Year 3 contains 30 EC of genuine free-choice/minor space, followed by diagnostics, professional skills, psychotherapy perspectives and a 15-EC empirical thesis. No specific minor or elective is invented.

alternatives.label: Child development in family, school & society
alternatives.concept: Combines developmental and social psychology, cognition, family and peer contexts, sociology, communication, ethics and empirical methods to study children and adolescents in the environments where they grow up. It is the closest feasible UCR response, while UCR lacks dedicated pedagogy, family-support practice, diagnostics and supervised clinical training.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed plan balances developmental psychology with family, school, peer and wider social contexts plus communication and research.
progression: Psychology, sociology, philosophy and communication foundations precede advanced development, assessment, cognition, social theory and research. All prerequisites and offerings pass; ten 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Developmental difficulties, mental health & youth support
alternatives.concept: Develops the programme’s complex-development and youth-support strand through developmental psychology, psychopathology, psychodiagnostics, health psychology, neuroscience, biology, resilience and research methods. It does not claim to reproduce UvA clinical qualification or supervised practice.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum gives sustained weight to developmental risk, mental health, assessment, biological context and evidence-based support.
alternatives.distinctness: Relative to the closest plan, this route replaces much of the sociology, communication and philosophy strand with biomedical foundations, public health, life science, ecology and advanced clinical-developmental psychology. Eleven courses differ, so the educational choice is substantially more health- and intervention-oriented.
progression: Brain, behaviour, biology and psychology foundations precede advanced clinical, developmental, biomedical and research courses. Formal prerequisites and offerings pass; eleven 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Children’s rights, families & social policy
alternatives.concept: Uses the programme’s family, social-environment, ethics, rights and policy evidence to organise sociology, political institutions, law, economic policy, gender history, inclusion and youth resilience around how society supports children and families.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed plan centres social structures, children’s rights, public institutions, inequality and policy responses affecting families and young people.
alternatives.distinctness: This route replaces most developmental, cognitive and clinical psychology courses with law, political science, public economics, social theory, gender history and policy. It differs from both earlier plans by well over 30 EC and treats child development principally through rights, institutions and social conditions.
progression: Introductory sociology, politics, law, economics and methods precede advanced rights, public policy, social theory and resilience work. All prerequisites and offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

candidates.label: Developmental difficulties, mental health & youth support

selection.assessment: The family–school–society plan is the closest feasible UCR response. The official complex-development/youth-support and family/social-context evidence also supports distinct health/clinical and rights/policy directions. All three are coherent, feasible and pairwise differ by more than 30 EC, so production stops at three.

notes.text: The UvA programme is a dedicated Pedagogical Sciences degree with compulsory family pedagogy, school learning, professional child-support practice, diagnostics, a bachelor internship and an empirical thesis. UCR can build strong developmental, psychological, social, ethical, policy and research foundations, but it does not reproduce the profession-specific pedagogical and supervised clinical-skills sequence.
